## Run-flat tire
A run-flat tire or run-flat tyre (RFT) is a pneumatic vehicle tire designed to resist the effects of deflation when punctured, allowing the vehicle to continue to be driven at reduced speeds for limited distances. First developed by tire manufacturer Michelin in the 1930s, run-flat tires were introduced to the public market in the 1980s.

plan.title: How to Change a Flat Tire Safely, Step by Step
plan.description: Learn how to change a flat tire safely, from pulling over to tightening the lug nuts. This step-by-step guide covers the tools you need and the common mistakes to avoid.

beats.narration: A flat tire never comes at a good time. But with about twenty minutes and a few tools, you can fix it yourself and get moving again. Here is how.

props.title: How to Change a Flat Tire
props.subtitle: Safe, simple steps anyone can follow

beats.narration: First, gather what you need. You want a spare tire, a jack, and a lug wrench. Check your owner's manual too, because it shows where your jack points are.
Step one is safety. Pull over to a flat, solid spot, well away from traffic. Turn on your hazard lights, put the car in park, and set the parking brake.
Never work on a slope or soft ground. The car could roll or the jack could slip. If you cannot find a safe spot, drive slowly to one or call for help.
Next, loosen the lug nuts. Do this while the tire is still on the ground. Turn the wrench counterclockwise, about half a turn each. Do not remove them yet.

props.alt: Loosening lug nuts with a wrench

beats.narration: Now place the jack at the jack point shown in your manual. Raise the car until the flat tire is a few inches off the ground. Never put any part of your body under the car.
Then unscrew the lug nuts the rest of the way and keep them together. Pull the flat tire straight toward you and lay it flat on the ground.

props.heading: Take the flat off
items: Lay it flat on the ground

beats.narration: Line up the spare with the wheel studs and push it on. Then hand-tighten the lug nuts. You should feel each one catch snugly before you go on.
Lower the car until the tire touches the ground, then tighten the nuts with the wrench in a star pattern. This spreads the pressure evenly. Finally, lower the car fully and remove the jack.

steps.label: Lower until the tire touches down

beats.narration: Many spares are temporary, so drive slowly and keep to the limit printed on the tire. Get the flat repaired soon. Also, check the spare's pressure at the first chance.

props.text: A spare gets you to a repair shop, not across the country.

coverage.reason: Covers the core sequence with safety, loosening before jacking and star pattern, but omits wheel chocks, torque spec/re-torque after 50 miles, and the check on hazards or removing hubcaps; there are few non-obvious facts.

structure.reason: Clean chronological chapters from preparation through safety, removal, mounting and aftercare, with no repetition.

hook_ending.reason: The opener 'A flat tire never comes at a good time' is a bland generic line, and the ending is a pressure-check instruction rather than a landing takeaway.

visuals.reason: Scene variety is good, but the highway traffic clip does not match the 'never work on a slope' narration, and the 'Inflated spare tire' checklist item is not spoken.

originality.reason: Largely generic how-to content with no surprising tips, such as wheel chocks, a loosen-first reason, or the cost of ignoring the temporary spare's limits.

instructions.reason: English, US-appropriate, about 2 minutes, and covers the steps; it misses torque and pressure follow-up detail that the brief expects.
